long.title: Why a Dim Blue Lamp Beats a Blinding Red One — in about a minute | Bear's Notes
long.description:
Aim the brightest red lamp you own at a metal plate — and not one electron escapes. Swap in a dim blue glow, and electrons fly off instantly. Crank the red to blinding and still — nothing.

A Brown Blue explainer, in the 3Blue1Brown tradition: concrete before abstract, mystery before formula.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
0:14 Light as packets
0:28 The escape cost
0:42 E = hν

The photoelectric effect in about a minute: light as packets whose energy is set by color, an all-or-nothing escape cost, and why color — not brightness — decides. The full explainer (leftover energy, threshold frequency, sodium by the numbers) is on the channel.

Source: Quantum Mechanics, Vol. 1, Ch. 1 — Why Classical Physics Failed.
